Continuar a conversa quando falta uma pa: Keep the conversation going when a word is missing: explain it in other words (paraphrase), ask politely for repetition and clarification, check what you've understood and buy time to think without going silent.
Você já sabe o que fazer quando falta um: You now know what to do when a word escapes you, when you haven't understood or when you need a moment to think. That's worth more than knowing lots of words: it keeps the conversation alive. Next lesson: tricky pronouns and prepositions.

Quando falta uma palavra: explique em ve: When a word is missing: explain instead of stopping
PASSO 1: se não souber uma palavra, não: STEP 1: if you don't know a word, don't stop or switch to English: describe it. The most useful formula is «Es una cosa que sirve para…» + infinitive (It's a thing you use for…): «Es una cosa que sirve para abrir botellas.» STEP 2: for a person, use «Es la persona que…»: «Es la persona que arregla los coches». For a place, «Es un sitio donde…»: «Es un sitio donde se compra pan». STEP 3: to compare, use «se parece a», «es parecido a» or «una especie de»: «Es parecido a una silla, pero más cómodo». STEP 4: to give the opposite, use «lo contrario de»: «Es lo contrario de barato». Note the preposition: «de», never «que» (English "the opposite OF"). STEP 5: to give the category, use «es un tipo de…»: «Es un tipo de fruta». STEP 6: to signal that the word is missing, say «No me sale la palabra» or «No recuerdo cómo se dice»; then explain. STEP 7: to rephrase, use «o sea», «es decir», «mejor dicho» and «en otras palabras»: «Llegué tarde; o sea, perdí el tren», «Fui el martes, mejor dicho, el miércoles». STEP 8: «cosa» is the all-purpose word ("thing"), and in speech you also hear «cacharro» (gadget) and «trasto» (piece of junk); in formal register prefer «objeto» or «aparato». STEP 9: don't invent words by mixing Spanish and English ("Spanglish"), such as «parquear» or «la troca» (fine in some US communities, but not understood everywhere): if in doubt, explain with simple words you know well.
em português dizemos «é uma coisa que se: English "It's a thing you use for…", "It looks like…" and "I mean…" have direct Spanish equivalents: «es una cosa que sirve para…», «se parece a…» and «o sea». The traps are the prepositions: "it looks LIKE / it's similar TO" = «se parece A», and "the opposite OF" = «lo contrario DE». And «o sea» is very common in speech, but shouldn't open every sentence — like "like" in English.
É uma coisa que serve para abrir garrafa: It's a thing you use for opening bottles.
It's a place where you buy bread.
It's the person who fixes cars.
É parecido com uma cadeira, mas mais con: It's like a chair, but more comfortable.
A palavra não me vem. É o que se põe na: I can't think of the word. It's what you put on the bed to sleep under.
I got there late; that is, I missed the train.
I went on Tuesday, or rather, on Wednesday.
«Servir para» indica a finalidade; «serv: «Servir para» expresses purpose; «servir de» means "to act as".
Escolha cinco objetos da sua casa e expl: Pick five objects in your home and explain each one in Spanish without saying its name: «Es una cosa que sirve para… Se parece a…». Ask a friend to guess.
Descreva em voz alta uma palavra que voc: Describe out loud a word you've forgotten, using «sirve para», «es lo contrario de» and «se parece a».
Pedir repetição, pedir ajuda e confirmar: Asking for repetition, asking for help and checking
PASSO 1: para pedir que repitam, use «¿P: STEP 1: to ask someone to repeat, use «¿Puedes repetirlo?» (tú) or «¿Puede repetirlo, por favor?» (usted). People also say «¿Cómo dices?» and «¿Cómo dice?»; in speech «¿Perdón?» or «¿Cómo?» is enough (like English "Sorry?" or "Pardon?"). In some countries, such as Mexico, you hear «¿Mande?» instead of «¿Cómo?». STEP 2: to ask someone to speak slowly, use «más despacio»: «¿Podría hablar más despacio?». Also: «más alto» (louder, "speak up") and «más claro». STEP 3: to say you haven't understood, use «No lo he entendido» or «No he entendido la última parte». To say you didn't hear properly, say «No te he oído bien»: «oír» is to hear the sound; «escuchar» is to listen; «entender» is to understand. STEP 4: to ask about a meaning or a form, use «¿Qué significa «cronograma»?», «¿Cómo se escribe?» (How do you spell it?), «¿Cómo se pronuncia?» and «¿Cómo se dice «schedule» en español?». There's no «de» after «significa». STEP 5: to check what you've understood, use «¿Quiere decir que…?» (Do you mean that…?), «Entonces, ¿…?», «A ver si lo he entendido: …» (Let me see if I've got this right) and «Si no me equivoco, …». After «a ver si», use the indicative. STEP 6: to ask for help, use «¿Me podría ayudar con…?», «Necesito ayuda con…» and «¿Le importa repetirlo?» (Would you mind repeating it?). STEP 7: pronouns: «¿Puede explicármelo?» and «¿Me lo puede explicar?» mean the same (lesson 60 gives the full rule). STEP 8: finish with «Gracias, ahora lo entiendo» or «Perfecto, ya lo tengo» (Great, got it). That signals the conversation can move on.
em português dizemos «pode repetir?», «m: English "What do you mean?" is «¿Qué quieres decir?», literally "what do you want to say?"; «¿Qué significa?» is for a word. "How do you spell it?" is «¿Cómo se escribe?». And English "I don't understand anything" is «No entiendo nada» — Spanish needs the «no» before the verb even with «nada».
«Devagar» não existe em espanhol: use «d: «Lentamente» is correct but sounds stiff in conversation; people say «despacio».
O pronome vai antes do verbo conjugado o: The pronoun goes before the conjugated verb or is attached to the infinitive, not in between.
Com «nada» depois do verbo, é preciso o: With «nada» after the verb, you need «no» before it.
Faça um diálogo curto: alguém fala depre: Make up a short dialogue: someone speaks fast and you (1) ask them to repeat, (2) ask them to speak more slowly, (3) ask what a word means and (4) check what you've understood with «Entonces, ¿quiere decir que…?». Play both parts out loud.
Peça em voz alta cinco coisas: repetir,: Ask for five things out loud: repeating, speaking slowly, explaining a word, checking and asking for help.
a verdade é que…: the truth is…, to be honest…
let me think for a moment.
PASSO 1: use um marcador curto no início: STEP 1: use a short filler at the start of your answer: «A ver…» (Let's see…), «Pues…» (Well…), «Bueno…», «Veamos…». They sound natural in Spanish. STEP 2: ask for time clearly: «Déjame pensar un momento» (tú), «Déjeme pensar un momento» (usted), «Un momento, que lo pienso». The verb «pensar» changes its vowel: «pienso», not «penso». STEP 3: repeat the question in your own words: «¿Que qué pienso del tema? Pues…» (What do I think about it? Well…). This buys time and shows you've understood. STEP 4: start with what you know: «La verdad es que no lo sé con seguridad, pero creo que…». Note: «la verdad es que» takes no «de». STEP 5: compliment the question: «Es una buena pregunta». STEP 6: if you make a mistake, correct yourself: «Perdón, quería decir…» (Sorry, I meant…) or «Mejor dicho, …». STEP 7: don't fill every silence with «eh…»; a «pues…» and a short pause are enough. In Mexico and elsewhere you hear «este…» as a filler, like English "um".
em português dizemos «bem…», «então…» e: English "Well…", "Let's see…" and "The thing is…" map onto «Pues…», «A ver…» and «Es que…». «Es que» introduces an explanation or an excuse («Es que no tengo tiempo» — The thing is, I don't have time). And English "um" or "uh" are not Spanish fillers: use «eh…», «este…» or «pues…».
O pronome vai colado ao imperativo, sem: The pronoun is attached to the imperative as one word, with a written accent.
Una comida complicada / Um almoço compli: Una comida complicada / A tricky lunch
Na quinta-feira passada tive um almoço d: Last Thursday I had a business lunch with some clients from Chile, and it was harder than I expected. When they asked me about the project timeline, the word «cronograma» wouldn't come to me, so I said: "It's the paper where you see what gets done each month." My boss smiled and helped me out. Then a client spoke very fast and I didn't understand a sentence, so I asked: "Sorry, could you repeat that more slowly?" To buy time before answering a difficult question, I said: "Let's see, let me think for a moment." In the end everyone laughed and the conversation got more relaxed. I learnt that you don't need to know every word: you just have to explain yourself and not go quiet.
Responda em voz alta a uma pergunta difí: Answer a difficult question out loud («¿Qué piensas del trabajo a distancia?») using a filler, a request for time and an explanation with «la verdad es que…».
Diga em voz alta uma frase para cada fun: Say out loud one sentence for each function: explaining a word, asking for repetition, asking someone to speak slowly, checking what you've understood and buying time.
